question: Should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103579 establish OpenClaw’s canonical durable approval lifecycle, with an explicit compatibility policy for existing timeout and fallback behavior?
rationale: This protected issue sets security authorization, persisted-state ownership, protocol shape, upgrade behavior, UI routing, channel actions, and session projection across an M4 stable core feature; automation cannot choose those permanent contracts.

options.title: Adopt staged architecture
options.body: Land the durable core after approving authorization and upgrade semantics, then review deep links/actions and channel/ancestry adoption in separate PRs.

options.title: Narrow durable scope
options.body: Persist records and lookup first while deferring shared resolution, timeout policy, or ancestor audiences to later design.

options.title: Retain surface-local flows
options.body: Improve modal, CLI, and channel approval paths independently without introducing a canonical durable approval object.

recommendation.title: Adopt staged architecture
recommendation.body: Land the durable core after approving authorization and upgrade semantics, then review deep links/actions and channel/ancestry adoption in separate PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored both the canonical umbrella proposal and the active implementation draft and have prior history in the existing lifecycle.
